why: RL has internalized the cue's deliberative-mode component, so nearly every RL answer opens on its own with cue-like tokens.
The RL-minus-base difference is about mode and termination (format, stopping), not about correctness, so few difference peaks sit at the first wrong step.

The base has the math and fails by uncalibrated stopping (premature wrong commits, non-terminating runs) that vary across samples, so a 4-sample vote recovers a clear part of the 42-problem gap rather than the ~1 point the literature gives.
Knowledge is not what the base lacks, so its pass@4 on the 328 reaches or exceeds RL's single-sample 206.
RL already contains the cue's component, so adding the cue to RL leaves it at its plain-prompt 463.
Code-RL carries only the generic cue-like component, which the cue already supplies, so Code-RL plus cue scores like the cued base (410) and gains nothing from the termination component.
Code-RL learned the domain-general deliberative-mode component, so even without the cue it lifts the plain base (224) a large part of the way toward the cued base (410).
RL's calibrated stopping makes its accuracy robust to truncating the sampling distribution, so min-p 0.1 leaves it at about 463.
The cued base's MATH-500 errors are mostly sample-specific termination failures, not missing knowledge, so a 4-sample vote recovers about half of the 53-point gap to RL.
Restarting cap hits before the vote removes the non-terminating runs as well, adding a few problems over the plain vote.
The base has the math for nearly every problem RL solves, so its pass@4 at T 1.0 reaches or exceeds RL's pass@1 of 463.
